- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast growth at 2–3% beyond peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.2), model frequently undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rebound.  
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., 1–3 days after sentiment shift); apply 1–2% lagged adjustment to forecast to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 70), model overestimates continuation; reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect reversion bias.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg 0.0–0.2), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence in “trend continuation.”
